subject: SIG: audit log ownership, incident retention & customer export options
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finbank.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: audit-team@finbank.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: audit log ownership & exports

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the earlier call. As part of our SIG review we're documenting how customers can access their audit trails and what retention guarantees Redwood provides for incident investigations. Can you confirm: 

- Where event logs are stored by default (region and storage service)?
- What the default retention period is for tenant event streams and whether it's configurable per-customer?
- The process and lead time for producing a tenant-level log export for security investigations (format, redaction approach, signed attestations)?
- If customers can set role-based access to their log exports, and if so what RBAC primitives map to export permissions?

If possible, please send a sample schema and any playbook we can reference for audit procedures. Our audit team would like to see the format ahead of the SIG deadline next week.

Thanks,
Olivia Chen
Security Assurance Manager — FinBank

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@finbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: audit log ownership & exports

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and attaching a short playbook + schema for the audit team. See attachments: export_playbook_v1.2.pdf and audit_log_schema.csv.

- Default storage & region: tenant event logs are written to encrypted object storage in the same region as the customer's primary deployment (AWS S3 in us-west-2 by default for your account). We also replicate critical telemetry to a centralized region for platform operations (encrypted at rest).

- Default retention: 90 days for high-fidelity per-request logs by default. This is configurable up to 3 years for Dedicated/Private customers via the retention parameter on the logging config. We provide a managed retention override for enterprise contracts (requires SLA addendum).

- Export process & lead time: We offer a tenant-level export delivered as gzipped newline-delimited JSON (ndjson) with a manifest (CSV) describing fields and hashes. Standard SLA for an unfiltered export is 3 business days; expedited exports (for incident response) can be delivered within 8 hours subject to availability and approval. Exports include a signed export attestation PDF. Redaction options: PII tokenization, payload hashing, and configurable field redaction (see redaction_matrix.xlsx).

- RBAC & entitlements: Exports are gated by the customer's admin role + an "Audit Export" entitlement. For Hosted accounts, the account owner or listed security contacts can request and approve exports. For Dedicated/Private we support integration with customer OIDC groups for fine-grained entitlement mapping.

Next steps: Kim (cc'd) will add a short note on the export API endpoints and authentication flow. Marissa will propose a checklist we can hand to your audit team for evidence review.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Security — Redwood Inference

Attachments: export_playbook_v1.2.pdf (23KB), audit_log_schema.csv (5KB)

Hi Olivia — adding the technical bits below. I'm pasting the important API examples; full OpenAPI spec is in the linked playbook.

1) Export API (tenant-level)
POST /v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/audit-exports
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Body params: {"start_ts":"ISO8601","end_ts":"ISO8601","redaction":"PII_HASH|TOKENIZE|NONE","format":"ndjson"}

Response: 202 Accepted + export_job_id; final artifact delivered to customer-specified S3 presigned URL or to a pre-configured customer S3 bucket (ACLs enforced).

2) Redaction & hashing
- PII_HASH: SHA256 salted per-tenant + rotation policy
- TOKENIZE: deterministic tokenization suitable for linkage tests (token map stored in HSM-backed vault)

3) Integrity & attestation
- Each export manifest contains per-file SHA-256 and an export attestation signed by Redwood KMS (certificate thumbprint provided).

4) Operational exceptions
- If an export contains platform-internal metadata that triggers security review, we fast-track it through Incident Response and provide a redaction summary within the 8-hour expedited SLA.

Let me know if you need example curl commands or a sandbox account to validate the workflow.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
